result.markdown: --- title: "Session 4 — Local Clusters and Hot Spots" subtitle: "Local Moran's I (LISA) · multiple testing · Getis-Ord Gi* · scan statistic · Lab 4" author: "Community Medicine Workshop" format: revealjs: theme: serif css: [../assets/slide_deck.css, assets/workshop.css, assets/quiz.css] include-after-body: assets/quiz-include.html embed-resources: true slide-number: true navigation-mode: linear code-copy: true center: false transition: fade width: 1280 height: 720 fig-align: center html-math-method: plain execute: echo: true warning: false message: false fig-width: 9 fig-height: 4.6 fig-dpi: 100 --- ## Where we are ::: {.incremental} - Session 3: the map **is** clustered (global Moran's I) - Today: **where**? Which blocks form hot spots, cold spots or are odd ones out? - By the end you can: - compute **local Moran's I** and classify **HH, LL, HL, LH** blocks - handle **multiple testing** - find hot and cold spots with **Getis-Ord Gi\*** - run and read a **spatial scan statistic** ::: # Topic 1 — Local Moran's I (LISA) {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## One statistic per area ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} loc <- localmoran(blocks$dengue_per_100k, lw, zero.policy = TRUE) head(round(loc, 3), 4) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Ii E.Ii Var.Ii Z.Ii Pr(z != E(Ii)) 1 -0.228 -0.001 0.016 -1.773 0.076 2 0.094 -0.007 0.132 0.277 0.781 3 -0.043 -0.052 1.923 0.006 0.995 4 0.403 -0.007 0.140 1.099 0.272 ``` ::: ::: | Column | Meaning | |---|---| | `Ii` | this area's local I: > 0 similar to neighbours, < 0 unlike them | | `Z.Ii` | z-score | | `Pr(z != E(Ii))` | two-sided p-value | ::: {.key} The **average of the local values equals the global I**: the global statistic is the average of the local ones (0.499). ::: ## Cluster types from the quadrant ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} z <- as.numeric(scale(blocks$dengue_per_100k)); lag_z <- lag.listw(lw, z, zero.policy = TRUE); p <- loc[, "Pr(z != E(Ii))"] blocks$lisa <- factor(case_when(p >= 0.05 ~ "Not significant", z > 0 & lag_z > 0 ~ "High-High", z < 0 & lag_z < 0 ~ "Low-Low", z > 0 & lag_z < 0 ~ "High-Low", TRUE ~ "Low-High"), levels = c("High-High", "Low-Low", "High-Low", "Low-High", "Not significant")) table(blocks$lisa) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` High-High Low-Low High-Low Low-High Not significant 11 10 1 0 57 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell output-location='slide'} ```{.r .cell-code} cols <- c("High-High" = "#d7191c", "Low-Low" = "#2c7bb6", "High-Low" = "#fdae61", "Low-High" = "#abd9e9", "Not significant" = "grey90") ggplot(blocks) + geom_sf(aes(fill = lisa), colour = "white") + scale_fill_manual(values = cols, drop = FALSE, name = NULL) + labs(title = "LISA cluster map (p < 0.05, unadjusted)") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](s4_local_clusters_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-4-1.png){width=900} ::: ::: ::: {.incremental} - **High-High:** hot spot. **Low-Low:** cold spot - **High-Low / Low-High:** spatial **outliers**, unlike their neighbours: check the data first - Here: a hot spot in the **south-east**, a cold spot in the **north-west**, one outlier ::: ## Multiple testing You ran **79 tests**: at 5%, about 4 blocks look significant by chance, and the tests are **correlated** (neighbours share neighbours). ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} c(unadjusted = sum(p < 0.05), fdr = sum(p.adjust(p, "fdr") < 0.05), bonferroni = sum(p.adjust(p, "bonferroni") < 0.05)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` unadjusted fdr bonferroni 22 13 3 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.incremental} - **FDR** (Benjamini-Hochberg) is a sensible default; **Bonferroni** is the strictest - Treat LISA as **exploratory**: it tells you where to look - The analytic p-values assume near-normal data; `localmoran_perm()` gives permutation p-values for skewed rates ::: # Topic 2 — Getis-Ord Gi* {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## Hot and cold spots directly Gi\* sums the values of an area **and its neighbours** (the `*` includes the area itself) and turns the sum into a **z-score**. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} lw_self <- nb2listw(include.self(nb), style = "B", zero.policy = TRUE) blocks$gi <- as.numeric(localG(blocks$dengue_per_100k, lw_self, zero.policy = TRUE)) blocks$gi_class <- cut(blocks$gi, c(-Inf, -2.58, -1.96, -1.65, 1.65, 1.96, 2.58, Inf), labels = c("Cold 99%", "Cold 95%", "Cold 90%", "Not significant", "Hot 90%", "Hot 95%", "Hot 99%")) table(blocks$gi_class) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Cold 99% Cold 95% Cold 90% Not significant Hot 90% 7 6 3 46 5 Hot 95% Hot 99% 1 11 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell output-location='slide'} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot(blocks) + geom_sf(aes(fill = gi_class), colour = "white") + scale_fill_manual(values = c("Cold 99%" = "#2166ac", "Cold 95%" = "#67a9cf", "Cold 90%" = "#d1e5f0", "Not significant" = "grey92", "Hot 90%" = "#fddbc7", "Hot 95%" = "#ef8a62", "Hot 99%" = "#b2182b"), drop = FALSE, name = NULL) + labs(title = "Getis-Ord Gi* hot and cold spots") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](s4_local_clusters_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-7-1.png){width=900} ::: ::: ## Gi\* or LISA? ::: {.key} **LISA** finds areas **similar** to their neighbours (hot or cold) **and outliers**. ::: ::: {.key} **Gi\*** finds where **high** (or low) **sums concentrate**: it separates hot from cold directly, but does not flag outliers. ::: ::: {.warn} Both run one test per area: apply the same **multiple-testing** caution. ::: # Topic 3 — The scan statistic {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## Kulldorff's circles Slide **circles of many sizes** over the map; for each ask whether it holds **more cases than expected from the population**. Reports the **most likely cluster**, its relative risk and a Monte Carlo p-value. Uses **counts and population** (Poisson), so no rates are needed. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} cen_km <- st_coordinates(st_centroid(st_transform(blocks, 32644))) / 1000 set.seed(5) sc <- scan.test(coords = cen_km, cases = blocks$dengue_cases, pop = blocks$population, nsim = 499, alpha = 0.05) summary(sc) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` nregions max_dist cases ex rr stat p 1 34 81.2 627 477.7 1.8 42.7 0.002 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.incremental} - Read: **blocks in the cluster**, **observed vs expected** cases, **relative risk**, **p-value** - The **maximum window** (default 50% of the population) changes what you find; choose it deliberately - Report the model (Poisson), the window, the number of simulations ::: ## Which local tool? | Question | Tool | |---|---| | Which areas are clusters or outliers? | **local Moran (LISA)** | | Where are hot and cold spots? | **Getis-Ord Gi\*** | | Is there one most likely cluster, from counts and population? | **scan statistic** | | Are the results robust? | other weights; adjusted p; compare methods | ## 🔧 Switch to R — Lab 4 {.lab-slide background-color="#1565c0"} ::: {.lab-box} **File:** `gis-workshop/labs/lab4_local.R` - `localmoran()` · classify HH / LL / HL / LH · map them - `p.adjust()` · `localG()` with `include.self()` - `scan.test()` and which blocks fall in the cluster ::: **Time:** 40 minutes · answer the Q questions in the comments ## Self-check quiz (1/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="s4q1" data-type="mcq" data-hash="op8h3n.yhxmmg" data-show="SXQgaGFzIGEgaGlnaCB2YWx1ZSBidXQgaXMgc3Vycm91bmRlZCBieSBsb3ctdmFsdWUgbmVp Z2hib3Vycw==" data-explain="SGlnaC1Mb3cgbWVhbnMgdGhlIGFyZWEncyBvd24gdmFsdWUgaXMgYWJvdmUgYXZlcmFnZSB3 aGlsZSB0aGUgYXZlcmFnZSBvZiBpdHMgbmVpZ2hib3VycyBpcyBiZWxvdzogYSBzcGF0aWFs IG91dGxpZXIgdGhhdCBkaWZmZXJzIGZyb20gaXRzIHN1cnJvdW5kaW5ncy4="} A block is classed High-Low (significant) in a LISA map. What does that mean? - It has a low value and is surrounded by high-value neighbours - It is part of a hot spot of several high-value blocks - It has a high value but is surrounded by low-value neighbours - Its p-value is too large for it to be classified ::: ## Self-check quiz (2/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="s4q2" data-type="mcq" data-hash="op8ucb.yhy13s" data-show="TWFueSB0ZXN0cyBhcmUgcnVuLCBhbmQgbmVpZ2hib3VyaW5nIHRlc3RzIGFyZSBjb3JyZWxh dGVk" data-explain="V2l0aCA3OSB0ZXN0cyBhYm91dCA0IHdvdWxkIGJlIHNpZ25pZmljYW50IGJ5IGNoYW5jZSBh dCA1JSwgYW5kIG92ZXJsYXBwaW5nIG5laWdoYm91cmhvb2RzIG1ha2UgdGhlIHRlc3RzIGRl cGVuZGVudC4gQWRqdXN0IChlLmcuIEZEUikgYW5kIHJlYWQgdGhlIG1hcCBhcyBleHBsb3Jh dG9yeS4="} Why should LISA p-values be adjusted or treated cautiously? - Local Moran's I can be calculated for a half of the areas at most - Many tests are run, and neighbouring tests are correlated - The p-values from localmoran() are always far too large to be used - LISA gives a single p-value for the whole map, not for each area ::: ## Self-check quiz (3/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="s4q3" data-type="mcq" data-hash="op97l1.yhyfl6" data-show="VGhlIGdsb2JhbCBJIGlzIHRoZSBhdmVyYWdlIG9mIHRoZSBsb2NhbCB2YWx1ZXM=" data-explain="V2l0aCByb3ctc3RhbmRhcmRpc2VkIHdlaWdodHMgdGhlIG1lYW4gb2YgdGhlIGxvY2FsIElp IGVxdWFscyB0aGUgZ2xvYmFsIE1vcmFuJ3MgSSwgd2hpY2ggaXMgd2h5IGxvY2FsIHZhbHVl cyAnZGVjb21wb3NlJyB0aGUgZ2xvYmFsIHN0YXRpc3RpYy4="} How are the local Moran values related to the global Moran's I? - The global I is the largest of the local values - They are unrelated statistics answering different questions - The global I is the average of the local values - The global I is the sum of the squared local values ::: ## Self-check quiz (4/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="s4q4" data-type="mcq" data-hash="op9ktr.yhyu2k" data-show="QSBkaXJlY3Qgc2VwYXJhdGlvbiBvZiBob3Qgc3BvdHMgZnJvbSBjb2xkIHNwb3Rz" data-explain="R2kqIHN1bXMgdmFsdWVzIG92ZXIgYSBuZWlnaGJvdXJob29kIHNvIGEgaGlnaCB6IG1lYW5z IGEgaG90IHNwb3QgYW5kIGEgbG93IHogYSBjb2xkIHNwb3QuIExJU0EncyBwb3NpdGl2ZSBJ IGRvZXMgbm90IGRpc3Rpbmd1aXNoIGhpZ2gtaGlnaCBmcm9tIGxvdy1sb3cgd2l0aG91dCB0 aGUgcXVhZHJhbnQu"} What does Getis-Ord Gi* give that local Moran's I does not? - A p-value for every block without any assumptions - A way to avoid choosing a spatial weights matrix - A correction for differences in population size - A direct separation of hot spots from cold spots ::: ## Self-check quiz (5/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="s4q5" data-type="mcq" data-hash="op9y2d.yhz8ju" data-show="VGhlIG1vc3QgbGlrZWx5IGNsdXN0ZXIsIHdpdGggaXRzIHJlbGF0aXZlIHJpc2sgYW5kIHAt dmFsdWU=" data-explain="VGhlIHNjYW4gc3RhdGlzdGljIHNlYXJjaGVzIGNpcmNsZXMgb2YgdmFyeWluZyBzaXplIGFu ZCByZXBvcnRzIHRoZSBtb3N0IGxpa2VseSBjbHVzdGVyLCBpdHMgb2JzZXJ2ZWQgYW5kIGV4 cGVjdGVkIGNhc2VzLCB0aGUgcmVsYXRpdmUgcmlzayBhbmQgYSBNb250ZSBDYXJsbyBwLXZh bHVlLg=="} What does the Kulldorff scan statistic report as its main result? - The most likely cluster, with its relative risk and p-value - A Moran's I value for each one of the circles that was scanned - The spatial lag of each of the blocks in the whole study area - The best neighbour definition for the spatial weights matrix used ::: ## Score and take-home **Your score: ** ::: {.incremental} - **LISA** gives each area a statistic, a p-value and a cluster type (HH, LL, HL, LH) - Many tests: **adjust** (FDR) and treat as **exploratory** - **Gi\*** separates **hot** from **cold** spots - The **scan statistic** finds the **most likely cluster** from counts and population ::: **Next:** Session 5: spatial regression and reporting

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
